extracted.intended_audience: researchers, research-integrity community, science journalists, and general readers interested in publication ethics
extracted.subtask_description: News-style reporting about an individual case of alleged research misconduct (fabrication, grant fraud) and its investigatory, legal, and publication consequences. Covers factual claims, precedents, and community reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applied for government grants using imaginary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Stapel is suspected of having applied for government grants using imaginary data, according to the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation that grant proposals must be based on genuine data; if proven, this supports criminal/administrative action and undermines the legitimacy of funded research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forgery via forged datasets in research and grant accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators also are exploring whether he is guilty of forgery by using forged datasets for research and in the written account of research grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using fabricated/forged datasets in publications or in grant documentation can be treated as forgery and may trigger criminal probes, seizure of records, and witness interviews (e.g., seizure of laptop, phone, financial administration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of faulty data in a federal grant request is a felony
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Individuals contemplating misconduct might be deterred by the knowledge that the submission of faulty data in a federal grant request is a felony punishable by jail time and/or a fine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal standard cited by a commenter: knowingly submitting false data in grant applications can carry felony charges and penalties including imprisonment and fines; this is a deterrent and grounds for prosecution in some jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals should retract publications when fraud is determined
rubrics_metrics.description: To date, journals have retracted 25 of Stapel’s published papers (by our count).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction is presented as the appropriate corrective action when fraud is established; however, follow-up practice matters — commenters note many fraudulent papers remained publicly available in repositories 'without a retraction notion', indicating repositories and publishers should ensure retraction notices and flags are applied and visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official committee classifications of misconduct ('fraud determined' vs 'fraud most likely')
rubrics_metrics.description: In the official count at http://www.commissielevelt.nl there are 46 journal papers identified in which ‘fraud has been determined’... and 7 journal papers where ‘fraud is most likely’, although Stapel does not agree with the last findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal investigations commonly produce categorical findings that affect which papers are retracted and what institutional/disciplinary actions follow; differing labels ('determined' vs 'most likely') influence the strength of remedial steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal prosecution and imprisonment are possible outcomes for fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: Should Stapel be convicted and jailed, he would join a pretty exclusive club. To our knowledge, only Eric Poehlman and anesthesiologist Scott Reuben have served time for offenses involving fabrication of data. In Reuben’s case, he spent six months in federal prison on charges of health care fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical precedents show that data fabrication has led to criminal convictions and prison sentences in some cases; this underscores the potential severity of legal consequences beyond academic sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentencing/outcome mitigation can be influenced by community support
rubrics_metrics.description: Luk Van Parijs had home detention and had to do community service; the judge was lenient thanks to several letters of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary indicates that letters of support, community standing, and other contextual factors can affect sentencing and penalties for researchers convicted or accused of misconduct; this is relevant for expectations about legal outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigatory procedure: seizure of devices and financial records; witness interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators have last month the laptop, the mobile phone and the financial administration of [Stapel] seized. These records are currently screened. 'The coming period will also have several witnesses be heard,' said a spokesman for the public prosecutor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard investigatory actions in alleged grant fraud/research fabrication cases include seizure of electronic devices and financial records and interviewing witnesses; such procedures are part of building criminal or administrative cases.
